narrative.overview: Ball IQ is a football quiz website that is the product, not a pitch for one. Every page is a list of things to play, arranged like a fixture list: what is on today first, then everything else you can find. One header, one frame, one accent spent only on Play and on a correct answer. Rebuilt on 2026-09-03 from a field study of thirteen quiz and sports-puzzle sites after the Scouting Report world and three editorial successors were rejected as generated-looking.
keyCharacteristics: Dark throughout on the app's own tokens; no gradients, glows, grain or lifted blacks.
One header for the website, the generated pages and the app in a browser; no call to action in it.
One card anatomy for today's puzzles, every game, clubs and lists.
Inter for everything read; JetBrains Mono only for in-game counters.
The browser owns the scroll; no sidebars or floating tab bars on the web.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Green means press this to play, or you got it right. More than one green control per screen means the page has stopped ranking its own actions.

rules.name: Grey-on-grey has a floor
rules.body: Nothing readable below 4.5:1; nothing user-facing under 12px.

rules.name: Sentence case everywhere
rules.body: Uppercase exists only in the 12px label. The condensed all-caps headline is the retired system's signature.

rules.name: One left edge
rules.body: Headings, prose, cards and tables share the 1200px frame's left edge; a narrow measure is never centred inside it.

rules.name: Depth is tone, not shadow
rules.body: bg → card → card-inset with a 1px border on anything pressable; the search dropdown is the only chrome shadow.

dos: Print the date and today's edition numbers on the homepage, and a checked date on every list.
Put every game, club, league and list on the page as a real link; the footer is a sitemap.
Keep SiteHeader.jsx and scripts/seo/shell.mjs in step by hand.
Show a club's colour as a dot or badge, from data.
Leave the rating empty until a player has answered something.
donts: Put a marketing button in the header, or store badges anywhere above the footer's last column.
Use a second display face, uppercase headlines, or monospace outside a game counter.
Add a glow, a gradient band, grain, or a tilted sheet.
Spend green on anything that is not Play or correct.
Print a question count, a fabricated rating, or an unmeasured people number.
Render an inner-scrolling shell, a sidebar or a floating tab bar on the web.
